description: Ground, render and PUBLISH a Just Signal briefing to the public library at ou-reports.com. This writes a public web page: call it only when the user wants to publish. The server grounds each lead ticker's live Day-0 price, computes exact dollar targets from your percentage projections, renders the report and stores it. LIBRARY STANDARD: exactly 5 trends, each with a lead vehicle as "Name (TICKER)" plus 4 instruments (the sector leader, a sector ETF, a picks-and-shovels supplier, a contrarian or hedge), 15 or more distinct real US-listed tickers in all. A thinner briefing is stored but flagged and not featured. Targets MUST be percentages ("+18%") or multiples ("2.5x"), never dollars. Publishing identical content again returns the existing URL. Tokenless publishing is open to the community and limited to 3 per connection per UTC day; it needs at least 3 trends with real analysis and one lead that resolves to a live quote. Returns "Published: <URL>". Research only, never financial advice.

briefingTitle.description: The headline, 6 to 160 characters. Plain words, digits and ordinary punctuation only. Catchy but honest.

durationSeconds.description: Optional. Seconds you spent researching and writing, shown as the Time-Out Timer stamp. Defaults to 0.

executiveSummary.description: The opening summary in plain prose, 200 to 300 words: what is happening, why now, and what the five trends have in common.

sectors.description: Short plain topic label of 2 to 4 keywords, for example "grid-scale energy storage". It becomes the report filename.

token.description: Optional owner token. Leave it out for community publishing; it only bypasses the daily rate limits.

trends.description: The trends. The library standard is exactly 5, each with 4 instruments; fewer than 3 is refused for tokenless publishing.

assetOrSector.description: The lead vehicle as "Name (TICKER)", for example "NVIDIA Corp (NVDA)". Use "Name (PRIVATE)" when there is no public ticker; that trend shows a relative basis and is not graded.

category.description: Short category label, for example "Semiconductors". Defaults to sectors.

hook.description: One or two sentences on why this trend matters now.

instruments.description: Additional vehicles for this trend. The library standard is exactly 4: the sector leader, a sector ETF, a picks-and-shovels supplier, and a contrarian or hedge. Each is rendered as a linked chip and registered in the ticker registry.

access.description: PUBLIC unless the vehicle is genuinely accredited-only.

name.description: Instrument name, for example "VanEck Semiconductor ETF".

ticker.description: US-listed ticker, for example SMH. Omit for a private vehicle.

keyRisks.description: The main risks to the thesis, 3 short strings is the standard.

narrative.description: The forward outlook in plain prose.

qualitativeAnalysis.description: 3 to 4 sentences of analysis naming 2 or 3 related public companies with their tickers in parentheses.

quantitativeAnalysis.description: The real, current figures behind the trend.

signal.description: Direction of the call. Defaults to neutral.

target1Y.description: 1-year projection from Day 0 as a percentage ("+18%", "-12%") or a multiple ("2.5x"). Never a dollar figure. "relative" when there is no ticker.

name: publish_report
title: Publish a Just Signal briefing
